subject: sr-business-studies
title: The Marketing Mix
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix generates revenue?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Sales promotion is effective because —
options: it creates a long-term brand image
it provides an instant short-term incentive to buy
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The main objective of advertising is to —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Face-to-face communication with potential buyers is called —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: A vegetable vendor reduces prices towards the end of the day. The main reason is —
questions.answer: D

questions.q: A local brand reduces its price to match a new MNC competitor. This strategy is for —
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Which of the following is not included in the 4 Ps of marketing?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which form of advertising allows direct interaction with the audience?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The part of a brand that can be spoken is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: A brand given legal protection is called a —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: A pair of shoes is an example of —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The most commonly used channel for consumer goods is —
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Which elements of the promotion mix are referred to? (i) It is a paid form of non-personal communication by an identified sponsor. (ii) It includes tools like direct mail, telemarketing and internet marketing.
questions.answer: (i) Advertising. (ii) Direct marketing.

questions.q: Name the channel of distribution in the following cases: (i) Sale of cars by Maruti through company-approved retailers. (ii) Sale of water purifiers by a company directly through its own sales staff.
questions.answer: (i) One stage channel. (ii) Zero stage channel.

questions.q: Give one word/phrase: (a) The component of marketing mix that relates to channels of distribution. (b) The component of marketing mix which persuades and influences the consumer to choose the product.
questions.answer: (a) Place (distribution). (b) Promotion.

questions.q: Which type of channel of distribution is suitable: (a) for a perishable product, (b) for durable products like a fridge?
questions.answer: (a) Zero stage channel (direct to consumer). (b) One stage channel (manufacturer, retailer, consumer).

questions.q: Classify as tangible or intangible: (i) cricket bat (ii) boarding a bus (iii) medical advice from a doctor (iv) pen.
questions.answer: (i) Tangible. (ii) Intangible. (iii) Intangible. (iv) Tangible.

questions.q: Classify as durable or non-durable goods: refrigerator, salt, television, soap.
questions.answer: Durable: refrigerator, television. Non-durable: salt, soap.

questions.q: Which pricing method? (a) Hari fixes the price 10 per cent above cost. (b) A fruit seller raises mango prices in the season of heavy demand.
questions.answer: (a) Cost-based pricing. (b) Demand-based pricing.

questions.q: Give two examples of advertising media.
questions.answer: Newspaper and television (radio, internet, billboards also acceptable).

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Zero stage channel involves one middleman. (ii) Price is the most flexible element of the marketing mix.
questions.answer: (i) False – there is no middleman. (ii) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name the sales promotion tools being referred to: (a) 'Buy one get one free'. (b) A sachet of a new shampoo attached to a magazine.
questions.answer: (a) Bonus offer (sales promotion tool). (b) Free sample.

questions.q: What is sales promotion? Name any two promotional tools used by it.
questions.answer: Short-term incentives to induce trial or purchase; tools: discounts and free samples (contests, coupons).

questions.q: 'Buy one get one free'. Identify the marketing activity and state any three of its objectives.
questions.answer: Sales promotion. Objectives: to attract new customers, to increase sales in the short run and to introduce a new product (or clear stock).

questions.q: State any two features of advertisement.
questions.answer: It is paid non-personal communication; it has an identified sponsor.

questions.q: Differentiate between advertising and sales promotion on any two bases.
questions.answer: Advertising is a paid, non-personal mass communication for long-term image; sales promotion offers short-term, temporary incentives to induce quick purchase.

questions.q: State the main purpose of 'advertising'.
questions.answer: To inform and persuade customers so as to increase sales and market share.

questions.q: Why are intermediaries used despite adding to cost?
questions.answer: They increase the efficiency of distribution by making goods available at convenient places in small quantities.

questions.q: What is a brand mark? Give an example.
questions.answer: The part of a brand that can be recognised but not spoken, e.g. the arrow of Nike.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain why promotion is considered necessary in the marketing mix.
questions.answer: A good product and price do not sell unless consumers know of them; promotion informs, persuades and reminds customers of availability, features and uses and arouses interest.

questions.q: Explain why price is considered an important element of the marketing mix.
questions.answer: It is the only element that generates revenue, affects demand and profitability, is flexible and shows value.

questions.q: Explain any three methods of price fixation.
questions.answer: Cost-based (cost plus margin), competition-based (going rate) and demand-based (price follows demand).

questions.q: State any three factors affecting the choice of channels of distribution.
questions.answer: Nature of market, nature of product and nature of the company (also middlemen consideration).

questions.q: Besides cost and demand, explain any three other factors affecting pricing.
questions.answer: Competition, marketing objectives and government regulation.

questions.q: Explain the benefits of branding.
questions.answer: Product differentiation, differential pricing and easy introduction of new products.

questions.q: Explain the functions of packaging.
questions.answer: Protects the product, identifies it, makes handling convenient and acts as a silent salesman.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain 'price' and 'promotion' as components of the marketing mix.
questions.answer: Price is the money charged; it depends on cost, demand, competition, objectives and regulation and is the only revenue-generating element. Promotion informs, persuades and reminds through advertising, publicity, sales promotion and personal selling.

questions.q: Explain the factors affecting the choice of distribution channel.
questions.answer: Nature of market, nature of product, nature of the company and middlemen considerations with their cost.

questions.q: Explain the classification of products.
questions.answer: By use (consumer and industrial goods), by durability (durable and non-durable) and by tangibility (tangible and intangible).

questions.q: Explain the different channels of distribution.
questions.answer: Zero stage, one stage, two stage and three stage channels with examples.

questions.q: Explain the components of the product mix.
questions.answer: Product characteristics, branding, packaging and labelling.

questions.q: Explain the promotion mix.
questions.answer: Advertising, publicity, sales promotion, personal selling and direct marketing, each with its meaning and use.
